progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: Entry knowledge: B11 (frequency = count over stated total, table and bar chart; allele frequency by copies; recessive phenotype frequency; SNPs; association, not cause; sample limits: size, representation, consistent definitions). Year 11 Working Scientifically: validity, reliability, graph conventions.
progression.startsWith: The hook: In one class, nine of the twenty-eight students who were counted have attached earlobes. Does that tell you how common attached earlobes are in everyone your age?
progression.stopsAfter: choosing a visible, non-sensitive, non-identifying characteristic and saying why it is counted, not converted to alleles; stating the agreement and anonymity rules; writing definitions with an "unsure" category before counting; describing an anonymous slip method with two counters; recording a tally table and calculating frequencies with a stated total; pooling classes and saying why the pooled value is a better estimate; drawing a column graph with correct conventions; explaining with a bead model why small samples scatter; identifying a trend, a pattern and a relationship (association, not cause); naming limitations and improvements to validity and reliability; using cautious language; applying all of it to the site's two-group earlobe task. SNP data analysis stays with B11.
progression.nextLesson: DNA sequencing and profiling for inheritance studies (route entry bio-m5-b12).

teaching.task: How do you collect, record and present data on how common a characteristic is, and how sure can you be about what it shows?
teaching.causalExplanation: (1) one class's count is not yet a population frequency: method, sample size and classification decide what it means (1); (2) the characteristic must be visible, quick, non-sensitive, and is not a one-gene trait, so it is counted, not turned into alleles (2); (3) data about people need agreement and anonymity, so no result can be traced and no one feels pressured (3); (4) definitions before counting, with an "unsure" box, because different judgements make the numbers mean different things (4); (5) unnamed slips and two counters reduce bias and counting errors (5); (6) frequency is count over total, and the total must be stated (6); (7) pooling gives a bigger sample and a better estimate (7); (8) separate categories go on a column graph with gaps, from zero, titled and labelled (8); (9) small samples scatter by chance; bigger samples land closer to the true value (9); (10) trend, pattern and relationship, with association not cause (10); (11) limitations, validity and reliability, and cautious wording (11).
teaching.conversationalApproach: Opens on the hook (hook (one class, one number)), then works through aim and choosing a characteristic, agreement and privacy, define the categories before counting, the method, record: the table and the frequency and the remaining scenes in order, with each reasoning stage shown on its own cue; ends with the unseen attempt (10 second countdown), brief feedback, the decision rule or board, and the key notes.
teaching.openingDecision: In one class, nine of the twenty-eight students who were counted have attached earlobes. Does that tell you how common attached earlobes are in everyone your age?
teaching.understandingCheck: group A 18 attached, 42 free; group B 30 attached, 30 free. Demands: frequency of attached in each group, compare, one limitation. Answer: A 18/60 = 30 percent; B 30/60 = 50 percent; attached more common in group B in these samples; limitation: 60 per group from one school is a small, possibly unrepresentative sample, so the difference could be chance. Crossed mistake: "18 / 42 = 43 percent" (divided by the other category, not the total).
teaching.curriculumScope: follows the chemistry practical format (chem-m5-p01.md, chem-m5-p03.md) and the Biology format and voice (bio-m5-b12.md). No pre-design pack exists for this route entry; this design works from the site extract ../site-extracts/bio-m5-l16.md and site lesson 16 (read 18 Oct: the frequency card with the earlobe populations, the "Sample quality and limitations" card, the four-step data interpretation sequence, the "Read the Table" earlobe task and the Analyse walkthrough). Route entry: bio-m5-p03 ("Collect and present population-frequency data", playlist order 21, practical-support branch, prerequisite bio-m5-b11, next bio-m5-b12). Route start: "Select a teacher-approved dataset or characteristics collection protocol." Route stop: "Prepare actual collection/recording/presentation and analyse trends, relationships and limitations; supplied data alone does not evidence learner collection." Route syllabus actions: B-frequency-collection, B-frequency-analysis. Syllabus (2017, p49): B5-IQ4-03 "collect, record and present data to represent frequencies of characteristics in a population, in order to identify trends, patterns, relationships and limitations in data, for example: examining frequency data; analysing single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)".

design.visualSystem: B11's coded frequency table and bar chart look, its "in this sample" tag style, its pool bar; B3b's coded gene-pool tray bead look for the bead population (round beads, painted bead plates below); the explainer kit (Plate, Callout, Mark, Countdown, HandText, DrawPath, scribbleEllipse, Enter); B6a's WrongChip, GreyTag, Cross, Cam. Shared plates from bio-m5-p01: m5x-clipboard-sheet-v1.png (tally sheet), m5x-pencil-v1.png. New coded items: the definition line diagram, the slip (three boxes), tally table, frequency calculation lines, column graph, bead sample chart (dot strip), analysis card (trend, pattern, relationship), limitations card, attempt card. - No human figures: slips fold and drop into the box by themselves; the mirror lies on a desk and shows only a soft highlight; counters are represented by two pencil tallies agreeing on the clipboard. No people.
design.transitionPlan: One class-collection workflow persists across the practical: the step rail along the top shows where the student is and the right zone holds one card at a time. The slips, table, pooled year group, column graph and bead model build in order, the analysis and limitation cards follow, the attempt card clears the board and feedback shrinks it to a strip; scene crossfade with settle.

scenes.teachingReason: Hook (one class, one number): In one class, nine of the twenty-eight students who were counted have attached earlobes.
scenes.narrationCue: Not yet / does and doesn't show
scenes.motionPurpose: A coded tally sheet on the painted clipboard (m5x-clipboard-sheet-v1.png) shows "attached: 9 of 28". On "everyone your age" the number zooms out to a wide coded field of small grey squares (abstract population, no people) with a "?" over it.
scenes.onScreenChange: the desk strip draws. A coded tally sheet on the painted clipboard (m5x-clipboard-sheet-v1.png) shows "attached: 9 of 28". On "everyone your age" the number zooms out to a wide coded field of small grey squares (abstract population, no people) with a "?" over it. On "Not yet" three chips write on under the field, one per cue: "how collected?", "how big?", "how judged?". On "does and doesn't show" the question writes on at the top left: "How common is it, and how sure are you?" Hold about 2 seconds.

scenes.visualReference: the aim card writes on in the right zone.
scenes.teachingReason: Aim and choosing a characteristic: The aim: collect data on how common a characteristic is in a population, present it clearly, and identify trends, patterns and limitations.
scenes.narrationCue: easy to see / not sensitive / one-gene trait
scenes.motionPurpose: On "easy to see" a checklist writes beside it: "visible", "quick to judge", "not sensitive", "can't identify anyone", each with a teal tick. Two candidate chips drop in: "earlobe shape" and "tongue rolling" (words only, no pictures).
scenes.onScreenChange: the aim card writes on in the right zone. On "easy to see" a checklist writes beside it: "visible", "quick to judge", "not sensitive", "can't identify anyone", each with a teal tick. Two candidate chips drop in: "earlobe shape" and "tongue rolling" (words only, no pictures). A crossed chip "health conditions" fades in (tag "sensitive: not for a class survey"). On "one-gene trait" a small grey tag writes: "many genes involved: count the characteristic; allele frequencies, see the roan cattle (B11)". Hold about 1 second.

scenes.teachingReason: Agreement and privacy: Data about people needs their agreement.
scenes.motionPurpose: Plan and agree". A coded plan card writes on: "teacher approval", "say what and why", "anyone can say no".
scenes.onScreenChange: step rail lights "1. Plan and agree". A coded plan card writes on: "teacher approval", "say what and why", "anyone can say no". On "say no" one blank slip stays on the desk, unticked, with the tag "no reason needed". On "no names" a painted blank slip (from m5x-slip-box-v1.png, item 2) enlarges with a coded "name: ___" line that takes a grey cross, leaving three tick boxes. Tag: "anonymous: can't be traced". Hold about 1 second.

scenes.teachingReason: Define the categories before counting: Next, write the definitions before anyone counts.
scenes.narrationCue: free / attached / unsure / test the definitions
scenes.motionPurpose: Define". The definition card writes in the right zone as a coded line diagram (no face, no head shape): in each of three panels, a vertical line tagged "side of head" and, beside it, a single ink outline of the lower half of an ear rim curving down into the lobe, with a pointer "earlobe" and a small dot "join point" where the lobe meets the line.
scenes.onScreenChange: step rail "2. Define". The definition card writes in the right zone as a coded line diagram (no face, no head shape): in each of three panels, a vertical line tagged "side of head" and, beside it, a single ink outline of the lower half of an ear rim curving down into the lobe, with a pointer "earlobe" and a small dot "join point" where the lobe meets the line. On "free" the first panel draws: the lobe rounds and hangs below the dot, the hanging part shaded teal and tagged "hangs below the join"; on "attached" the second: the rim runs straight into the line at the dot, amber outline, tagged "joins directly"; on "unsure" the third: a short lobe barely below the dot, grey, tagged "in between". On "judge the same earlobe differently" two coded tick marks land in different boxes for the same grey curve, with a pen "?" between them. On "test the definitions" three small practice outline curves appear under the card with two coded tick rows beneath; two ticks agree, one pair disagrees and the definition line "hangs below the join" gains an underline (tag "sharpen the wording"). Hold about 1 second.

scenes.motionPurpose: Collect". The painted slip box (m5x-slip-box-v1.png, item 2) sits centre-left; the hand mirror (m5x-hand-mirror-v1.png, item 1) lies on the desk with only a soft highlight in its glass.
scenes.onScreenChange: step rail "3. Collect". scenes.teachingReason: Record: the table and the frequency: Record the counts in a table: category, tally, count and frequency.
scenes.narrationCue: thirty / which total / thirty-two per cent
scenes.motionPurpose: Record". The table writes in the right zone (B11 table look): columns "category / tally / count / frequency (%)"; rows "attached / IIII IIII / 9", "free / IIII IIII IIII IIII / 19", "unsure / II / 2", "total slips / 30".
scenes.onScreenChange: step rail "4. Record". On "which total" the 30 and a new "classified: 28" ring with a "?"; on "Leave out the unsure slips" the unsure row greys and a table footnote writes: "frequency of the 28 classified (2 unsure left out)". scenes.teachingReason: Pool the year group: One class is a small sample, so pool the results from four classes.
scenes.narrationCue: pool / twenty-seven per cent / better estimate
scenes.motionPurpose: On "pool" the four tally sheets slide together into one. On "jump around" the four percentages pulse in turn; on "better estimate" the pooled row rings teal with the tag "bigger sample".

scenes.teachingReason: Present: a column graph: To present it, use a column graph, because the classes are separate groups, not points on a continuous scale.
scenes.motionPurpose: Present". A small tag on "column graph": "column graph (a bar chart with vertical bars)".
